title: Strict left-Koszul completion and its normalized Roos coordinates
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, a scheme $T$, the completed integral coefficient sheaf $R$ [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers], and its uniformizer section $\pi$ [def-sp-completed-uniformizer-section]. On unbounded $R$-complexes use the principal Koszul tower $L_j=[R\xrightarrow{\pi^{j+1}}R]$ with transition $(\pi,1)$ [def-pur-principal-koszul-quotient-towers]. Define the strict functor $P\mapsto (L_j\otimes P)_j$ and its composite $C$ with the existing Roos functor $\mathsf R$ [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Its unit is the shifted-cone lift of the product of the degree-zero inclusions $1\otimes x$, with zero shifted homotopy. The Koszul transition naturality makes this a valid chain map. The zero and one Roos coordinates are the unshifted cone projection and the shifted cone projection, each followed by a product projection. For a tower $Q$, the column tower is $j\mapsto\mathsf R_n(L_j\otimes Q_n)$; row and column coordinates are the four composites of these two projections, with output degrees $k,k-1,k-1,k-2$. These are the constructions and conventions used in the power-torsion limit theorem.
